text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers are accurate and match the card and tool outputs (24.2% vs 2.6%, 63% low complexity, 30 charts, 0 of 11 below billed, 9 of 26 data-without-tests). The leaning is cautious and the headline is clear. But the summary has several weaknesses: it repeats itself, includes an unsupported interpretive leap, and gives weak next steps. The cited examples do not support the main claim.","problems":["Speculation that 'notes are written up to match the bill' is not supported by the evidence; 9 of 26 lacking a lab on the claim is weak, since data review can be of external records or independent historian, and the claim is not tied to any claim.","Parenthetical '(e.g., URI or back pain billed 99215 with 'high' MDM)' is generic; only C0082872 (R10.9) and C0083037 (M54.50) are documented 'high' in the card, and neither is URI. The example is loosely grounded and not cited.","Cited claims C0082819 and C0082837 have no documentation on the card and do not illustrate the data-review-without-test finding or the documentation-supported finding; better picks would be documented examples like C0082872 or C0083037.","Redundant text: risk-adjusted score and the 63% figure are each stated twice, which pads the rationale.","Next steps are vague and don't name the 9 notes with data review but no test; they ask for a larger sample while the records exchange was complete with 30 of 30 usable charts, so 'too thin' is questionable. They also omit a coder review of specific claims, despite the rationale saying a coder should check.","Does not flag that 11 documented 99215 claims is a small sample, nor that the 63% low-complexity share conflicts with the charts supporting high MDM, leaving the tension unresolved."]}
